script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for March 20. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.

Inside nearly every cell in your body is a complete instruction manual for building you.  Three billion letters, encoding everything from your eye color to how your neurons wire.  This manual is DNA—and you carry it everywhere.

DNA uses only four chemical letters—A, T, G, and C. Three billion letters, arranged in specific sequences, spell out every gene. Different sequences create different proteins. The complexity of life emerges from just four characters. Humans are 99. 9% genetically identical.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: Information precedes form.  DNA teaches that complex outcomes begin as coded instructions.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Information Encoding - What Are You Writing?.

Here's your activity: DNA encodes instructions that persist. What 'instructions' are you encoding in others through your example, your words, your patterns? Consider one message you're consistently sending—intentionally or not. Is it what you want to transmit? This helps you consider what information you're encoding in others.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about your body's instruction manual can be applied to information encoding - what are you writing?. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
